title: A second Marīnid army, 3,300 under Muṣliḥ al-Dīn, attacks Khālid's 8,100 at Málaga and is broken: 2,440 of theirs lost for 370 of ours
The Mamlūk army, 5,650 with Valencians beside them, attacks Osman's 3,870 at Jerez and is thrown back: 3,110 lost against 845
Six days later Khālid avenges the Mamlūks at Jerez: 7,260 Granadans against Osman's 3,015, of whom 1,870 fall, for 173 of ours
A Marīnid army of 3,380 under Aghlab lands in al-Gharb. Khālid marches west and destroys it at Beja: 2,260 of theirs lost for 480 of ours
After several more battles, Morocco is nearly beaten by June 1370. The victory has cost a great many lives
source: Trent's account (by June 1370; no save yet; the battles will be filled in from the save at the peace)

title: The last battle of the war, at Mālaqa. 8,370 Granadans meet 2,890 Moroccans and break them: 1,040 of theirs lost for 154 of ours
source: Trent's screenshot of the battle report (12 September 1370)

title: Peace with Fās. Morocco gives up the whole north shore of the Strait, eleven towns: Ronda and Marbella, and the nine of its puppet Kingdom of Sevilla, which ceases to exist, from Cádiz and Jerez to Gibraltar, Tarifa and Algeciras. Morocco also pays reparations and signs an agreement against piracy. With its ṭāʾifas, Granada now holds all 72 towns of the Strait's three lands

warDead.note: battle losses from 22 battles; Granada's total of about 13,000 is from Trent's war screen and includes attrition

source: saves of 13 September 1370 and 1 July 1370; Trent's screenshot of the terms

title: After the peace the realm is 60 towns and 749,000 people, 368,000 Sunnīs to 333,000 Catholics. The estate loans of 1369, 469 dīnārs, are still owed. Expenses are 144 a month against an income of 63 while the mercenaries are still on the books

data.treasurySources: Trent: the war chest came mainly from bullying the estates, Moroccan concessions, bullying the vassals, and Egypt

title: Twenty-one years after the Peace of Qurṭuba, the lands of the great river are coming back: Andalusīs have gone from 7% to 33% of their people, and Muslims from 8% to 25%. Twelve towns of the valley are Andalusī by culture, and Qurṭuba is Muslim by faith. Ishbīliyya has gone from 14% Muslim to 31%, Jayyān from none to 30%

data.note: the 1370 figures include the north shore, taken from Morocco and already mostly Muslim

source: the extracted checkpoints of 4 June 1349 to 13 September 1370

title: The world at the peace of Fās: Granada stands 13th among the powers of the world and is a Regional Power, 16 points short of the last Great Power (Bohemia, 46). Castile is 8th, its ally Egypt 7th, Morocco 11th; France and England, 4th and 5th, lead Christendom. The Ottomans hold Constantinople, and no war touches Iberia or the Maghrib

data.greatPowers: the nine ranked above the first Regional Power

the Ottomans against Karaman and the Anatolian beyliks (from 10 October 1369)

title: The Battle for the Strait is over: the Throne of Granada endures. Qashtāla has stopped sending demands, Fās has failed to cross, and the throne in Gharnāṭa has the same occupant it began with. Granada stands free

effects: Consolidated Governance for 100 years: +0.5% monthly control, +25% speed of integration
Al-Andalus can be formed while holding fewer Iberian territories
the Reconquest of Iberia can be fabricated at reduced cost
every location held in Granada, Andalusia and Murcia raised to core integration
every ṭāʾifa being annexed gains 25% annexation progress
enables the decision Usher in the Golden Century, which starts the Golden Century situation

source: Trent's screenshots of the event (14 September 1370)

title: The day the Strait is won, the sultan's brother Ismāʿīl ibn Yūsuf, sixteen, is married to Hippolyte of Villa di Chiesa, eighteen, a Sunnī Sardinian, daughter of Xavier, lord of Cagliari, a vassal of Tūnis. The old royal marriage of 1354 has lapsed, and this one takes its place

data.bride: Hippolyte (game name), born 1352, Sardinian culture, Sunni

title: The sultan begins to absorb the Ṭāʾifa of Mursiyya into the realm. The annexation runs at 1.4 a month and stands at 2.8 on 1 November. Qashtāla takes a claim to prevent it, and Mursiyya one to resist it
The dīwān begins to draw up the claim for the Reconquest of Iberia against Qashtāla, the war goal the victory in the Strait opened. By 1 November it is 44% made

data.name: Reconquest of Iberia
data.unlockedBy: the variable can_reconquer_iberia, set by the outcome of the Battle for the Strait (Across the Pillars)

title: Maryam bint Ismāʿīl leaves the integration of the new lands and joins Duʿā in promoting Andalusī culture: both seats of the dīwān now work for the Call

Seven weeks after the peace the mercenaries are paid off: expenses fall from 144 a month to 71, against an income of 73, and the treasury holds 156. The seven estate loans are still owed. Granada has opened its granaries to Egypt and the three ṭāʾifas, and rises to 12th in the world

data.world: Morocco rises to 10th (37 points); Egypt and Tlemcen have stood down the hosts raised for the war (Egypt from 60,600 men under arms to 1,700, Tlemcen from 11,300 to 30)
